To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diagnostic values of LH and FSH as well as LH /FSH ratio at time points during GnR test were evaluated using power logistic processes, and the results of this study may provide a reference for the diagnosis and treatment of patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
the mathematical model of GnRH-III was developed and validated by logistic processes.
the mathematical model developed based on autoregressive logistic processes is useful to predict the concentration of LH and FSH in lamprey.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical modeling and simulation of the lamprey LH and FSH secretion using autoregressive logistic processes.
the study of the lamprey gonadotropins and the GnRHs.
the mathematical modelling of GnRH-III in the regulation of LH and FSH secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GnRH- III is not a selective FSH-releasing factor in mammals and the diagnostic values of LH, FSH and LH/FSH at different times points during the GnRH test are not suitable for the evaluation of GnRH function in mammals.

GnRH- III has a weak effect on the release of FSH, LH, and LH/FSH in the mammalian pituitary gland, but the GnRH-III has a significant effect on FSH, LH and LH/ FSH ratio in the lamprey pituitary gland.
GnRH- III is an agonist for FSH in the human and in the rat, but it is not an agonist for LH, and it is not a selective agonist for FHS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GnRH- III can be used as a diagnostic tool in the assessment of the GnRH test, especially when GnRH-III was administered at 0.1 μg/kg.
the mathematical model of GnRH-III was successfully developed based on autoregressive logistic processes.
GnRH test is useful in assessing pituitary gonadotropins reserve in patients with hypogonadism, but it is not useful in evaluating the pituitary gonadal axis reserve in patients with hypergonadism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mathematical models can be used to describe the dynamics of gonadotropins secretion in response to GnRH-III.
the mathematical models of the GnRH test can be used to describe the dynamics of FSH and LH secretion and to predict the response of LH/FSH to GnRH stimulation in mammalian species.
mathematical models can provide a framework to understand the complex dynamics underlying GnRH-III regulation in lamprey.
